symptom: safety rules did not fire on MCP tool names like gmail.send_message, so a send would have been allowed as an ordinary call
root_cause: rules matched on raw tool names, but real tool names are dot/underscore/slash separated; the matcher assumed prose
detection: unit tests written before the rule was wired (the test was the detector)
fix: normalise name separators to spaces before matching, and widen the money rule to plan-change verbs
prevention_rule: any policy matcher must be tested against the real naming shapes of at least three brokers (MCP, Composio, Arcade) before it is merged. Enforced by tests/test_policy.py::test_safety_rules_gate_by_name.

root_cause: human decision (kill switch, incident, or travel)
fix: nothing to fix; resume only after the reasons in plan.md §8 are met
prevention_rule: a paused venture never runs: the worker refuses any run whose venture is paused, and the Sentinel denies every action for it

symptom: a read of a billing portal (read billing portal) was gated as a payment, so the demo showed 4 pending approvals of which 2 were harmless reads
error: safety rules matched on the object of the action rather than its first verb
root_cause: rules matched any money word anywhere in the name; OpenBot own convention is that the action is its first verb and a word naming what it acts on does not count. I had departed from the convention we claim to share.
detection: reading the seeded demo output: a read was waiting for a human
fix: READ_VERBS list; a read-only first verb skips money/comms/publish/share rules but never credentials or deletes
prevention_rule: an approval queue that fills with harmless reads gets ignored, and an ignored queue is a stopped company. Rules match the first verb, and reads about money are browsing. Enforced by test_reading_about_money_is_browsing_not_moving_money and test_a_read_cannot_skip_credentials_or_deletes.
